blockers.quote: The auto pulls away. Through its back window, counters over three heads on the lane: the neighbour watering plants, the paan-stall owner, the kid on a cycle; the rest of the lane is a blank flat layer.
blockers.why: The viewer's week: the first people the counter lands on, besides mom, are a neighbour, a paan stall and a kid. None of that is chai, the bus or metro, exams, the office, or family.
blockers.fix: > SCENE: The bus pulls away. Through its window, counters over the chai-stall owner and your cousin at the stop; the rest of the lane is a blank flat layer. In line 17, replace "An auto-rickshaw idles at the gate." with "The bus waits at the stop."

suggestions.quote: By the time he left school? 93% (c01).
suggestions.fix: I would leave here. The skip just landed, then a school statistic starts while you sit still. Replace lines 127-130 with: "Your strip is thinner."

suggestions.quote: In one taste test, students were told, "This is your last chocolate."
suggestions.fix: Cut this line and line 54. Go from "Maybe it's not just the chai." to "You almost go back for another glass. Then it wouldn't be the last."

suggestions.quote: The same doorway through the seasons, a second and a half each: the monsoon, you dripping under an umbrella; Holi, colour on both your faces; winter, a shawl; summer, mangoes on the step.
suggestions.fix: Cut the four matching hellos. Hold 2 s on the winter doorway, counter at 257, and cut to Grandpa's chair.
Replace with: "Thirty-eight. You came home anyway."

keep.quote: You're not at the start of your time with her. You're at the tail end.
It wasn't her clock. It was your timetable.
Saying no isn't a plan. A ticket is.
